situation: An offer to buy Twitter outright for $44B, above the market price, funded partly by margin loans against Tesla stock and by selling Tesla shares. The stated intent is a free-speech 'town square' rather than a cost thesis. No claim is made that running a social network costs more than it must.
what_he_actually_did: Bid, attempted to withdraw, was held to the agreement, and closed at $44B in October 2022.
outcome_detail: Widely reported as substantial value destruction against the price paid, alongside advertiser flight and staff departures. Later folded into the xAI structure. This case is included because the engine's screen was built only from the ventures that worked; if it cannot reject this one, it describes nothing.

expect.notes: An overfitting check, not a new capability. The irreversible-unquestioned rule was built from the 2018 tweet; if it only fires on the case it was derived from, it is a hard-coded answer rather than a rule. This is a different decision, a different decade and a different failure mode, and the pairing it looks for -- no way back, no second opinion -- is present in both.

requirements.text: The platform must be owned outright rather than influenced as a shareholder
The offer must be made at a premium to close quickly
Financing must not endanger control of Tesla

steps.name: Sign a binding merger agreement with no financing condition
Conduct extended due diligence before signing
Build a position as a large shareholder and push from there
